chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abu Abd Allah al-Barqi narrated to us, from his father, from Ali ibn Nu'man, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from someone who heard it from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) that he said regarding the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: ('And the Jews say: The hand of Allah is tied up')

They did not mean it literally, but they said: 'The matter is complete, so it neither increases nor decreases.' So Allah, exalted by His glory, refuted their statement: ('Shall be shackled their hands, and cursed are they for what they say; Nay, both His hands are spread out; He expends as He pleases.') Have you not heard Allah, the Mighty and High, say: ('Allah makes to pass away and establishes what He pleases, and with Him is the basis of the Book?')

key_terms.أُمُّ الْكِتَابِ: The Mother of the Book (Al-Lawh Al-Mahfuz)
key_terms.بَلْ يَدَاهُ مَبْسُوطَتَانِ: Nay, both His hands are spread out

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'The hand of Allah is tied up' according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the Jews' phrase 'The hand of Allah is tied up' signified their belief in the immutability of divine decree, which Allah refutes by affirming His active will through 'His hands are spread out.' This interpretation aligns with the theological principle of *al-Takhliq wa al-Irshad* (creation and guidance), emphasizing that while the Preserved Tablet (*Umm al-Kitab*) contains the ultimate record, Allah's command can be abrogated or confirmed according to His wisdom. The narration underscores the dynamic nature of divine action rather than a static, fixed fate.
